study type: randomized open label parallel group study
exposure: intravenous morphine followed by oral codeine
outcome: time to first spontaneous bowel movement
cohort: 80 women undergoing elective caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia
finding: In a multimodal protocol for postoperative analgesia after caesarean section, better pain control and lower opioid intake was observed in patients receiving oral oxycodone as compared to those on intravenous morphine followed by codeine.
